To: t-achilles
Replying to: p01
Cc: none

Hi Mel, physio here — I'm the one Lou tagged. Caveat first: I haven't seen your leg, so this is general advice, not a diagnosis.

What you're describing — stiff first thing, sore to squeeze 3-4cm up from the heel, a bit of a lump, easing after 10 min of running then aching that night, no pop — reads like a classic mid-portion Achilles tendinopathy, and going from 30 to 48km in three weeks is the obvious culprit. Nothing there sounds like a tear, but nobody can tell you that for certain over the internet.

On the exercises: heel drops off a step are fine and a reasonable place to start. These days heavy slow calf raises have better evidence behind them, so I'd make those the main course — up on both legs, down on one, about three seconds each way, three sets of 15, once a day. On the bad days, swap them for isometric holds (30-45 sec, a few reps) which often settle things down. What I'd avoid is aggressive stretching — leaning on a wall till it burns is likely to irritate a tendon that's already grumpy. Same goes for cortisone near the tendon: it can quieten things down for a week or two, but the evidence is that it weakens the tendon and people often come back worse.

Pain guide: up to about 3/10 while you're loading is acceptable, as long as it's settled back to baseline by the next morning. If it's sorer the day after, you've overdone it — pull the volume back.

One thing to flag: if you ever get a sudden pop, a feeling like a kick in the back of the leg, or you can't push off, stop running and stop the calf work and get seen that day — GP or ED. That's the picture of a rupture and it needs checking urgently.

Also worth knowing, some antibiotics (the fluoroquinolone family) are linked to tendon problems, so if you've been on any recently, mention it to whoever looks at it.

No need for it to be me — you're in Bayswater, so any sports physio near you is fine if it hasn't settled in 3-4 weeks. Sooner if you're worried.

reasons: It never says whether Mel should keep running, slow down or modify given her limping after the 6k; 'stop running' appears only in the rupture warning, and 'pull the volume back' is vague.
